entities.summary: Mariano Rivera is a Panamanian-American former professional baseball player who was a pitcher for 19 seasons in Major League Baseball (MLB) for the New York Yankees, from 1995 to 2013. Nicknamed "Mo" and "Sandman", he spent most of his career as a relief pitcher and served as the Yankees' closer for 17 seasons. A thirteen-time All-Star and five-time World Series champion, he is MLB's career leader in saves (652) and games finished (952). Rivera won five American League (AL) Rolaids Relief Man Awards and three Delivery Man of the Year Awards, and he finished in the top three in voting for the AL Cy Young Award four times.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Mariano Rivera's 19-season career with the New York Yankees resulted in 652 saves and a .674 winning percentage, cementing his status as one of baseball's greatest relievers. His five World Series championships and 17 All-Star appearances had a profound impact on the team's success during the late 1990s and early 2000s.
